assessment_summary: The statement is false. The bound (5n - 10)/3 applies to planar graphs with girth at least 5 (i.e., all faces have at least 5 edges on their boundary). However, the statement only requires the graph to contain 'at least one cycle', which does not rule out cycles of length 3 or 4. Any simple planar graph containing a triangle or a 4-cycle can easily exceed this bound. Therefore, the statement is demonstrably false.
counterexample: Let G be the complete graph K_3 (a triangle). G has n = 3 vertices and 3 edges. G is a connected planar simple graph and contains a cycle. According to the statement, G can have at most (5(3) - 10)/3 = 5/3 edges. Since 3 > 5/3, G violates the statement, providing a concrete counterexample.
flawed_step: N/A (The statement itself is false and has no proof provided)
